definition: The low-frequency vibration — approximately 8 Hz — felt through the soles of the feet when standing over an active Pulse corridor. A physical sensation of the world's circulatory system moving beneath you. Named for the way it registers in bone rather than ear: not a sound but a pressure, a reminder that the network runs below and does not stop for you.
origin: Zone 3 Gray Zone vernacular; absent from any corponation documentation
usage: Used by Gray Zone residents, maintenance workers, and anyone who lives or works above Pulse infrastructure. Carries connotations of exclusion — you feel the Pulse because you cannot ride it.
example: "Couldn't sleep again. The thrumline was going all night — Chicago to somewhere, someone going somewhere. Not us."
